thread:
Maria (CSE): hey team, onboarding check-in for BlueForge — they're hitting bursts of 429s from the browser embed during initial ramp. noticed it when several QA engineers open the app at once.
Jordan (Dev): rough. which SDK/version?
Maria (CSE): web-embed-sdk v0.8.2, ephemeral tokens rotated every ~30s. calls to /v1/embeddings (batch size 1) from multiple tabs -> fanout. 429 body: `{\n  \"error\": \"rate_limit_exceeded\",\n  \"retry_after\": 3\n}`
Sam (Eng): are these preflight (OPTIONS) spikes or actual POSTs?
Maria (CSE): POSTs — we see the api_key preflight hits too but most fail with POST 429s.
Jordan (Dev): can you paste a minimal repro we can run locally?
Maria (CSE): sent logs to the thread but here's a quick curl from a repro machine:```\ncurl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <EPHEMERAL>\" \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-embed-1\",\"input\":[\"test\"]}' -v\n```
Jordan (Dev): thanks. I ran it twice in parallel and saw 1/3 responses 429. repeating with keep-alive off/on?
Evan (SRE): common pattern: lots of short-lived ephemeral tokens + many tabs => backend sees many unique auth handshakes and can't aggregate. also connection churn kills keep-alive reuse. two quick mitigations: bump pilot key rate cap temporarily; advise client to reuse tokens per session (longer TTL) or spike-protect at SDK.
Maria (CSE): customer is ok with a short bump if we can guarantee no regressions. account id BG-1234. they ramp tomorrow morning UTC. can we do temporary whitelist? :pray:
Evan (SRE): I can open a temporary soft-bump to allow x5 for 24h. will need exact window. set for 2026-04-02 08:00-20:00 UTC?
Maria (CSE): yes, that'll cover their QA window.
Sam (Eng): longer-term we should change edge preflight caching and increase TTL for ephemeral keys when seen from same Origin+ClientID. quick SDK change: reuse ephemeral token across tabs by writing to sessionStorage and passing an \"x-rw-session\" header. e.g.:```\n// in embed SDK\nconst token = sessionStorage.getItem('rw_ephemeral') || await fetchToken();\nsessionStorage.setItem('rw_ephemeral', token);\nfetch('/v1/embeddings', { headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}`, 'x-rw-session': 'bf-qa-1' } })\n```
Jordan (Dev): will add a debounce for concurrent embedding calls and batch where possible. also fallback to queued retries with jitter on 429. sample backoff: retry-after * (1 + rand()).
Maria (CSE): customer asked if server-side proxy is recommended — they have an SSR layer.
Evan (SRE): yes, server-side proxy with single long-lived token per session is ideal. reduces fanout massively. if SSR not available, the SDK sessionStorage approach helps.
Jordan (Dev): repro logs attached: several distinct ephemeral token values within 10s window -> confirms fanout.
Sam (Eng): I'll push a change to the gateway to extend token bind TTL per origin for known onboarding keys and add a short cache for preflight responses (10s). that should cut the thundering-herd.
Evan (SRE): done: raised soft-cap for BG-1234 to x5 from 08:00->20:00 UTC tomorrow, monitoring alert created. will roll back automatically after 24h. alert id: RB-4472.
deploy-bot: deployment rwd-gateway@v2.14.3 started by Sam — ref RB-4472.
Sam (Eng): small deploy with preflight cache and session affinity header. rolling now.
Maria (CSE): thanks all! I'll tell BlueForge the plan and ask them to enable the sessionStorage change and debounce. will follow up after tomorrow's window. :thumbsup:
Evan (SRE): please ping here if 429s persist and include a sample span id.
Maria (CSE): will do. tagging @BlueForge (PM) in the customer email.
Jordan (Dev): noted for SDK release notes — include guidance on ephemeral token reuse and recommended retry pattern.
Maria (CSE): closing loop after the ramp. thanks :wave:
